newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Bomb destroyed in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Bomb destroyed in Northern Ireland.

text.p: British army experts on Friday blew up a large car bomb, the first detected in Northern Ireland since an IRA truce on July 20.
Police said the bomb was in a car abondoned at a hotel in Lisbellow in County Fermanagh late on Thursday night. They said a telephone warning was received but could give no further details.
Army experts carried out a controlled explosion on the vehicle and examination showed it was carrying between 500 and 1000 lbs of home-made explosives.
No group claimed immediate reponsibility for planting the bomb.
The Irish Republican Army called a halt to its 28- year war against British rule of Northern Ireland last month, enabling its political arm, Sinn Fein, to join peace talks.
But two radical, small Irish repubican groups have opposed the ceasefire and one, the Irish Nationalist Liberation Army, said it would not observe a truce.
